title: Food Systems, Nutrition, and Health

sections.credentialOverview:
Credential Overview

The Bachelor of Science degree in Food Systems, Nutrition, and Health provides students with a rigorous scientific foundation for understanding the complex intersections and relationships among food, policy, labor, social justice, economics, the environment, culture, and population health. Graduates will have competency in food systems, nutrition, public health, social and economic equity, and sustainability, as well as strong scientific preparation to address a wide range of food systems and nutrition issues and prepare for graduate and professional education in nutrition, public health, food systems, and related fields.
sections.credentialAdmissionRequirements:
Admission Requirements

• Minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA

• Course requirements: 

• NUTR 200 or equivalent

• One biology or chemistry course from the following: BIOL 118, BIOL 180, CHEM 120, CHEM 142, CHEM 143, CHEM 145

• 5 credits of English composition (minimum 2.0 grade)
sections.credentialCompletionRequirements:
Completion Requirements

General Education requirements

Basic Skills

• Written and Oral Communication (15 credits)

• English Composition: 5 credits from the University list

• Writing: 10 credits from the University list

• Reasoning (RSN) (5 credits): 5 credits from the University RSN list

• Diversity (DIV) (5 credits): 5 credits from the University DIV list

Areas of Inquiry

• Arts and Humanities (A&H) (10 credits): chosen from the University A&H list

• Social Sciences (SSc) (10 credits) 

• Economics (5 credits): one of ECON 200, ECON 201, FISH 230/ECON 230, ESRM 235/ENVIR 235/ECON 235

• 5 additional credits from University SSc list

• Natural Sciences (NSc) (20 credits) 

• Biology (5 credits): BIOL 118 or BIOL 180

• Chemistry (5-6 credits): one of CHEM 120, CHEM 142, CHEM 143, CHEM 145

• 4-5 additional credits from University SSc list

• Additional Areas of Inquiry (25 credits): courses from the University A&H, SSc, NSc lists to bring total to 65 credits

Major Requirements

85-86 credits

• Supporting Sciences (25 credits): minimum 25 credits of science courses from supporting sciences list; see adviser or department website for list of approved courses

• Research Methods & Technologies (9-10 credits): 

• Statistics (4-5 credits): one of BIOST 310, QMETH 201, Q SCI 381, STAT 220, STAT 221/CSSS 221/SOC 221, STAT 290, STAT 311

• Methods (5 credits): one of NUTR 202 (recommended), GEOG 425, SOC 300

• Food Systems Core (31 credits): NUTR 200, NUTR 302, NUTR 303, NUTR 402, NUTR 412, NUTR 493

• Upper Division Electives (20 credits): see advisor or department website for list of approved courses

• Minimum 46 credits of upper-division courses
